title: merge-queue-triage: stacksFor() counts a stacked ejection as an independent hit when the stack runs through a green, non-victim queue group
body:
Filing gate: ① a defect with a named location, measured once on real queue runs. Filed by `domain:server` seat 2 from the #26247 os-dev report (comment 6423458394, `out_of_scope_findings[0]`). ⛔ Not a claim.

**Business reason.** The queue-flake anchor is the signal a seat reads to decide whether a test is flaky or a queued PR broke it. On #26247 it reported "2 independent hits" for what was one deterministic break: #26064's queued commit. That nearly sent the reading to "flake" and to the wrong owner. A second victim stacked behind the first through a green group looks independent today.

**Reader who acts.** The owner of `.github/workflows/merge-queue-triage.yml` (governed path; Tier H).

## Measured

- `stacksFor()` unions two victims only when one victim's base equals another victim's head. On #26247, #26198's queue base `7122b0db` is the head of #26210's group, whose base `745c276b` is #26158's group, whose base `17f21e8d` is #26064's victim head. #26210's and #26158's groups were green because their affected-only `merge_group` Test Core never selected `plugin-security`, so neither is a victim, and the chain was not walked.
- The dev reproduced the break: `17f21e8d` failed 0/10 on the one test, `main` passed 40/40, and #26064's patched head passed 10/10.

## Expected

- `stacksFor()` walks base to head through every `merge_group` run in the window (the index `stackEdges` already builds), not only through victims, so a victim whose base chain reaches another victim's head is counted as stacked. No extra API calls are needed.
- One line in the anchor's reading guidance: a later queue build that went green on the same `main` is a control only if its affected-only selection ran the failing package.

## Dedupe

Searched this repo (open and closed) for "merge-queue-triage stacksFor independent stacked transitive base chain": #26247 (the anchor this came from), #4859 and #10128 (the workflow and its aggregation), none this defect.
